+#: They track what is open right now (how deep the ``with`` blocks are,
+#: the resources to close, the child contexts) and not what the user
+#: set, so putting back an older value would leak a resource or close
+#: one twice.
+_STATE_NOT_RESTORED = frozenset({"_depth", "_exit_stack", "_child_contexts"})
+
+#: Public names a snapshot may use for the private attributes.
+_STATE_ALIASES = {
+    "protected_args": "_protected_args",
+    "opt_prefixes": "_opt_prefixes",
+    "meta": "_meta",
+    "parameter_source": "_parameter_source",
+}

+def _deepcopy_state(value: t.Any) -> t.Any:
+    """Deep copy one value of a context snapshot.
+
+    A value ``copy.deepcopy`` cannot copy, such as an open file or a
+    lock held in ``Context.obj``, is shared with the snapshot instead of
+    making the snapshot fail. A plain dict is copied key by key when its
+    whole copy fails, so that one such value does not take the
+    isolation of the others with it.
+    """
+    # Imported here, since importing click should not load copy.
+    import copy
+
+    try:
+        return copy.deepcopy(value)
+    except Exception:
+        if type(value) is dict:
+            return {key: _deepcopy_state(item) for key, item in value.items()}
+
+        return value
+
+
+def _copy_state_value(name: str, value: t.Any) -> t.Any:
+    """Copy the value of one context attribute for a snapshot or for
+    putting one back: deeply for the user's data, one level for the
+    other lists, sets and dicts, and not at all for anything else
+    (commands, parents, callbacks), which a snapshot only refers to.
+    """
+    import copy
+
+    if name in _STATE_DEEP_COPIED:
+        return _deepcopy_state(value)
+
+    if isinstance(value, (list, set, dict)):
+        return copy.copy(value)
+
+    return value
+
